name: ETF Common Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary and are subject to change.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline for most scholarships was March 15, 2026 (applications opened December 15, 2025). A few funds use separate windows.
apply: Create an account in the ETF scholarship portal (Grant Interface), complete the ETF Common Scholarship Application to be matched, then answer each matched scholarship's added questions.
eligibility: East Tennessee students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Some funds consider need and ask for a FAFSA Submission Summary or Federal Student Aid Estimator results; students who cannot file a FAFSA because of immigration or citizenship status remain eligible for many programs. Awards notified by about July 1.

name: NDCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (200+ college, statewide, county and community funds); NDCF awards $1,000,000+ in scholarships. Amounts vary; some funds award under $500.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund. Many statewide funds accept applications January 1 to April 1; the pages do not state the year, so confirm for 2027.
apply: Apply to each scholarship separately per its page; many use the NDCF scholarship portal (Grant Interface) and some use mailed forms.
eligibility: North Dakota students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules; some require an essay.
notes: Each fund has its own application; do not reuse answers across applications. Deadlines are firm.

provider: The Community Foundation for McHenry County
name: CFMC scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary (listed awards from $2,000 to $8,000 total).
deadline: Most scholarship opportunities open November 30, 2026, and close January 31, 2027. Some funds use other windows.
apply: Log in to the CFMC Scholarship Portal, take the eligibility quiz for each scholarship, and complete the full application if eligible.
eligibility: Students in McHenry County, Illinois (northwest Chicago suburbs); many funds are tied to specific high schools. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Chosen as the Chicago-area portal: The Chicago Community Trust does not run a public student scholarship application. Notifications in late March and early April 2027.

name: CFNEIA scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; 253 awards totaling over $800,000 in 2024 (average about $3,164). Amounts vary; some are renewable.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted. The application window opens January 10 with the deadline typically in mid-March; the 2025 deadline was March 12, 2025, 8 p.m.
apply: Complete one common application online at cfneia.org/scholarships with transcript, activities summary, essay and a letter of recommendation. Some funds require extra materials or apply through schools.
eligibility: High school seniors, college students and adult learners in the foundation's 24-county Northeast Iowa region (including Black Hawk, Benton, Bremer and Winneshiek). Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Selection weighs financial need, academic performance, field of study and community involvement.

name: QCCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (60+ applications); more than $500,000 a year, most recently $856,327.
deadline: Opens November 1, 2026. Most scholarships due February 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m.; Quad City Regional Auto Show scholarships due January 17, 2027.
apply: Apply free through the QCCF online scholarship system (Grant Interface), which matches students to scholarships they qualify for.
eligibility: Students in the Quad Cities region of Iowa and Illinois, including affiliate areas. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: LCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (93 funds); 299 recipients and over $606,000 in 2025. Listed awards range from $400 to $5,000.
deadline: The next cycle opens December 15, 2026. The portal-wide deadline is not posted; the Student Success Scholarship lists March 15, 2027.
apply: Complete the General Application in the LCF AcademicWorks portal, then apply to recommended opportunities.
eligibility: Mainly Lancaster County, Nebraska students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Award values may change before the cycle reopens.

name: Wichita Foundation scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; listed awards range from $400 to $5,000.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 cycle opened January 1, 2026, with applications due March 31, 2026, unless otherwise noted.
apply: Complete the general application in the Wichita Foundation Scholarship Portal (Grant Interface), then answer added questions for each matched scholarship.
eligibility: Kansas high school seniors (statewide funds) and students at Wichita-area and other named schools. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules; several set minimum unweighted GPAs of 2.0 to 3.0.
notes: Most funds weigh financial need, academics, activities and an essay; FAFSA required for need-based awards.

provider: Boreal Waters Community Foundation (formerly Duluth Superior Area Community Foundation)
name: Boreal Waters scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships; more than $800,000 to students each year.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted. The 2026 cycle opened December 1, 2025, and closed February 24, 2026, 11:59 p.m.
apply: Take the eligibility quiz in the online portal to be matched with scholarships, then complete those applications.
eligibility: Students living in northeast Minnesota or northwest Wisconsin who plan to attend a college, university, community or technical college, or trade school. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: No test scores required.

provider: Community Foundation for the Fox Valley Region
name: CFFVR scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (over 300); over $2 million a year.
deadline: Most applications open December 14. 2027 deadlines range from February to October by scholarship.
apply: Create an account in the CFFVR Scholarship Portal (Grant Interface; do not use a school email) and apply to scholarships you qualify for.
eligibility: High school seniors, homeschooled, college and non-traditional students in the Fox Valley region of Wisconsin and affiliate areas (Brillion, Chilton, Clintonville, Shawano, Waupaca). Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Many funds consider financial need; complete the FAFSA first where required. No limit on applications.

name: CICF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; 211 scholarships totaling $2.1 million in 2024.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund; many 2027 windows run November 2026 to February 2027 (some October 2026 to January 2027).
apply: Create an account on the CICF SmartSimple scholarship portal, complete your profile, and submit each scholarship application by its deadline.
eligibility: Mainly Indianapolis and central Indiana students; some funds require Indiana residency or a specific county or school. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules (for example, a 2.5 minimum GPA or upper third of class).
notes: Applicants gather financial information (FAFSA, income). The Lilly Endowment Community Scholarship is listed separately.

name: Cleveland Foundation Scholarships (via College Now Greater Cleveland)
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 60); amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. Applications open in December and are due in March; the 2026-27 General Application is closed.
apply: Apply through the Cleveland Foundation Scholarships General Application administered by College Now Greater Cleveland.
eligibility: Mostly graduating high school seniors; many funds require Cuyahoga, Lake, Geauga or Lorain county residency or specific schools. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules; GPA minimums range from 2.0 to 3.5.

name: ScholarshipCONNECT
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 300); $3.6 million to 1,497 students with the Dayton-Montgomery County Scholarship Program in the most recent year.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. Applications open in mid-December and are due at the beginning of March; the 2026-27 deadline was 4 p.m. on Friday, March 6.
apply: Submit the ScholarshipCONNECT general application, then choose individual opportunities with added requirements on the Opportunities tab.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and current college students in the Greater Dayton region (Montgomery, Miami, Greene, Darke, Preble and northern Warren counties). Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Some funds are merit-based without need. Not for graduate or professional programs.

name: St. Louis Community Foundation scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (80 programs); more than $2.5 million to over 700 students last year.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund; most listed scholarships are open January to April. Confirm 2027 dates.
apply: Most opportunities are on the My Scholarship Central portal: register, complete an eligibility profile, and apply to matched scholarships.
eligibility: Students in the St. Louis region and Missouri. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFO scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (about 450 funds); nearly $1.7 million to about 950 students for 2026-27. Awards range from $250 to $10,000; many renew for two to four years.
deadline: Opens January 1, 2027, for 2027-28; the 2027 deadline is not yet posted. The 2026 deadline was Monday, March 16, 2026.
apply: Complete the universal application at cfozarks.org/applyforscholarships, which matches you to funds.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and college students in the Missouri Ozarks region. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFNIL scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (over 125); $500K+ awarded.
deadline: Three cycles each year: Fall, November 1 to January 1; Winter (main), December 1 to February 1; Spring, March 1 to April 1. The page does not state the year.
apply: Complete one universal application per cycle in the CFNIL portal (Grant Interface); answers auto-match you to eligible scholarships.
eligibility: High school seniors and older, mainly in Boone, Jo Daviess, McHenry, Ogle, Rock, Stephenson and Winnebago counties (Rockford area), with some funds open USA-wide. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: KZCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships and education grants (more than 60); amounts vary and can cover full cost of attendance.
deadline: Application window is December 1 through March 1 every year.
apply: Complete one universal application in the Kaleidoscope portal to be matched with scholarships.
eligibility: Kalamazoo County residents and high school graduates. Open regardless of citizenship or permanent residence status. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: FAFSA required, but KZCF supports students ineligible to file it.

name: TGKVF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (over 100 funds); awards from $1,000 to $12,000, average about $3,000. Over $1.6 million to 500+ students in 2024-25.
deadline: 2027-28 application dates not yet posted; the 2026-27 deadline has passed.
apply: Apply through the TGKVF Scholarship Portal (Grant Interface).
eligibility: West Virginia residents statewide, high school seniors and up, attending in-state or out-of-state two-year, four-year, vocational or graduate programs; homeschool students eligible. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Students usually receive only one TGKVF scholarship. Volunteer reviewers recommend awards; notifications in May.

name: CFGA scholarships (universal application)
value: Hundreds of scholarships each year through many donor funds; amounts vary by fund (for example, the Jim Kennedy Scholarship for children of Cox employees is up to $40,000 split over 8 semesters).
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. For the 2026-27 cycle, most scholarships opened December 8, 2025 and closed March 2, 2026.
apply: Complete the universal application on the Foundation's GrantInterface portal to see which scholarship programs you can be considered for.
eligibility: Students planning full-time post-secondary enrollment. Each fund sets its own rules; examples include the Nancy Penn Lyons Scholarship (Georgia residents, 3.0+ GPA, SAT 1000+ or ACT 22+) and the Mayor's Youth Scholarship (Atlanta Public Schools graduates or City of Atlanta residents).
notes: Several funds are employer-, college- or HBCU-specific. Renewal applications are sent separately to current recipients.

name: CFSA scholarships
value: More than 40 scholarship funds; amounts vary by fund.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-2027 scholarship cycle is closed.
apply: Create an account in the Foundation's scholarship application portal (GrantInterface) and apply to open funds; review the FAQ document and available-scholarships list first.
eligibility: Each fund sets its own residency, school, major, merit and need rules; the application page does not list general criteria.
notes: The official page gives few details; check the available-scholarships list when the next cycle opens.

name: Common Scholarship Application
value: 25+ scholarship opportunities through one application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application ran December 1, 2025 to February 3, 2026.
apply: Submit the Community Foundation Tampa Bay Common Scholarship Application on the GrantInterface portal (one application per year during the window).
eligibility: High school seniors, college and technical school students, and people returning to school, primarily from Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco, Hernando and Citrus counties. Individual funds set their own criteria.
notes: The Foundation also points students to Apply Tampa Bay for broader scholarship matching.

provider: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
name: Coastal Community Foundation scholarships
value: 50+ scholarship programs for high school seniors; examples include Amanda's Scholarship Fund ($5,000 per year, renewable) and the Rufus C. Barkley, Jr. Leadership Scholarship ($10,000 per year, renewable).
deadline: The application window opens in mid-January and closes in mid-March; exact 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Create an account on the online portal, which matches you to scholarships you qualify for. Submit short-form personal and financial information, a transcript, letters of recommendation and essay answers.
eligibility: Mainly residents of Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester counties, with some funds for other areas. Each fund sets its own rules (for example, the Hebrew Orphan Society N. Edgar Miles Scholarship requires top 25% of class, a 3.0+ GPA and financial need; the Barkley award is based on academic merit and character).

name: HRCF undergraduate scholarships
value: More than 80 undergraduate scholarships through one online application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The official page describes a December 1 to March 1 application window with April email notifications.
apply: Submit one online application in the scholarship portal to be considered for multiple scholarships.
eligibility: Students who graduated or will graduate from a South Hampton Roads high school. Most scholarships require financial need and full-time enrollment; some are limited to high school seniors.
notes: Mostly need-based. The how-to-apply page still references an older cycle, so confirm dates.

provider: The Community Foundation of Frederick County
name: CFFC scholarships
value: More than 200 scholarships for Frederick and Carroll County students; amounts vary.
deadline: Schedule posted as 2026-2027: post-secondary/general scholarships open March 1 and close March 31; music and athletic scholarships open September 1 and close September 30; trades/certifications open November 1 on a rolling basis. Confirm the year on the official page.
apply: Create an account and apply in the Foundation's NextGen online scholarship system; gather the documents listed in the Scholarship Applicant Guidebook first.
eligibility: Frederick County residents for most funds (Trumpower scholarships for Carroll County residents): high school seniors, current post-secondary students and nontraditional students age 21+.
notes: About 60% of the scholarships consider financial need.

name: LCCF scholarship program
value: About 16 named funds; awards from $400 to $10,000 per year, some renewable for up to three more years. 45 scholarships were awarded in 2026.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026-2027 cycle opened November 3, 2025 and closed February 23, 2026 at 4:00 pm.
apply: Apply once through the Scholarship America online application to be considered for all matching funds; include a current transcript and SAT/ACT scores if not on the transcript.
eligibility: Lancaster County high school seniors, current Lancaster County residents or graduates of a Lancaster County high school enrolling full-time at an accredited US college, university, vocational or trade school. Minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale (some funds require 3.0).
notes: Selection considers academic record, leadership and financial need.

name: CFNJ Scholarships Universal Application
value: More than 135 scholarship funds; more than $2 million to 271 recipients in the most recent year. Examples: James Moody Jazz Scholarship ($5,000 annually), Daniel McKinney III Memorial Scholarship (up to $20,000 over four years).
deadline: Open and close dates vary by scholarship; 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Fill out one universal application on the CFNJ GrantInterface portal, then review and apply to the scholarships you may qualify for. Some funds are not on the universal application.
eligibility: Mostly graduating high school seniors; each fund sets its own residency (for example Greater Newark, South Jersey counties or specific high schools), GPA (some require 2.5 or 3.0) and need rules.
notes: Evaluation generally weighs academics, activities, community involvement, work and financial need.

name: RACF Consolidated Scholarship Application
value: 125+ scholarships, 55+ of them through one Consolidated Scholarship Application; awards from $1,000 to $13,000.
deadline: The consolidated application runs December 1 to February 28 each year; each scholarship lists its own deadline. 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Complete the Consolidated Scholarship Application in the RACF Scholarship Portal and upload an unofficial transcript, a letter of recommendation and required essays; some scholarships use separate applications.
eligibility: Almost all scholarships are for Rochester area residents; funds set their own school, major and other rules.
notes: RACF considers financial need (cost of attendance above expected family contribution); grades count but are not the only factor.

name: FCCF scholarships
value: More than 150 scholarship funds; 445 scholarships totaling $1.7 million in fiscal year 2025. One application considers you for up to 4 scholarships.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application ran January 8 to April 15, 2026 (extended).
apply: Apply online through the Scholarship America portal with an official transcript, FAFSA Submission Summary (Student Aid Index), essay and letter(s) of recommendation.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors or current college students who live in, are native to, graduated from or attend high school in Fairfield County. Minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA (some funds require 3.0 or higher). Applicants must show financial need.
notes: Need-based program. Competitive senior awards focus on the Greater Bridgeport area; other funds run through high school guidance offices. Undocumented students are told to contact the Foundation.

name: GWCF scholarship application
value: More than 140 scholarship opportunities through a single application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application opened December 1 and closed February 25, 2026. Decisions are released in early May.
apply: Submit one online application with a transcript, short answer, essay and optional recommendations (required for certain funds); you are matched to funds automatically. FAFSA is not required.
eligibility: Mostly high school seniors from the 60 cities and towns of Worcester County who will enroll full-time in a 2- or 4-year undergraduate program; some funds serve college students, adults or non-residents.

name: Common Scholarship Application
value: 150+ scholarship opportunities through one application; awards from $1,000 to more than $5,000, some renewable.
deadline: 2027-2028 dates not yet posted. The 2026-2027 deadline was March 4, 2026 at 2:00 p.m.
apply: Complete the Common Scholarship Application (short essays; some funds need recommendations or supplements) plus a FAFSA, CA Dream Act Application or Federal Student Aid Estimator result.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors, current undergraduate or graduate students and adult re-entry students who have lived in San Diego County at least one full year. Minimum 2.0 GPA; most funds require 2.0 or 2.5. Undocumented and international students may apply for funds not limited to citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Many funds consider financial need, including middle-income families. Some funds interview in April.

name: SRCF scholarships
value: Dozens of scholarships; awards from $400 to $10,000, some paid annually over multiple years. Over $1,000,000 went to 400 students last year.
deadline: Most scholarships open in December and close in March; 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Create an account (personal email) on the SRCF AcademicWorks portal, complete the general application, then submit the recommended scholarship applications with transcript, FAFSA or CA Dream Act confirmation, essay and recommendations.
eligibility: Students from El Dorado, Placer, Sacramento, Sutter and Yolo counties (varies by fund). GPA requirements range from 2.0 to 4.0+ depending on the fund.
notes: Most scholarships are need-based; merit funds emphasize GPA.

name: EPIC Scholars Application
value: Over 90 scholarship opportunities; amounts vary.
deadline: Most applications open December 1 and close February 24; individual scholarships vary. 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Complete the EPIC Scholars Application (formerly the universal application) on the GrantInterface portal to be matched; some scholarships need separate applications. Upload a transcript; some funds need recommendations or essays.
eligibility: High school seniors, current college students and returning adults; each fund sets its own residency, GPA and other rules. Most require full-time enrollment.
notes: The Legacy Scholarship is a separate process for high school juniors in Bexar or Webb counties.

name: ACF scholarship general application
value: Over 60 scholarship opportunities; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 application opened January 15 and closed March 25 at 11:59 p.m. CT.
apply: Complete one general application to be auto-matched, then answer supplemental questions; submit transcripts, short answers and recommendations for select scholarships.
eligibility: Central Texas students pursuing higher education (graduating seniors, college and vocational students); each fund sets its own criteria.

name: WCCF Common Scholarship Application
value: 38 donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 Common Application opened January 1, 2026 and closed February 15, 2026; the Clough Fellows Scholarship deadline was March 15, 2026.
apply: Create an account on the GrantInterface portal and complete the online Common Scholarship Application for personalized scholarship matches.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and returning adults in western Colorado (including Delta, Eagle, Garfield, Mesa, Montrose, Ouray, Rio Blanco, San Juan and Montezuma counties). Funds set their own rules, for example the Bill Patterson Scholarship (Mesa County, 3.75+ GPA, science or engineering).
notes: Mix of merit, need and combined funds.

name: Innovia scholarships
value: Over 50 scholarships; individual awards $500 to $4,000; over $400,000 awarded each year.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-27 application opened December 3, 2025 and closed March 4, 2026.
apply: Complete a short eligibility questionnaire, create a MyInnovia account and submit one application with a personal statement; file the FAFSA or WASFA.
eligibility: High school seniors and graduates from Innovia's 20-county service area in Eastern Washington and North Idaho going to accredited college or vocational/technical programs. GPA minimums vary by fund (commonly 2.5 to 3.5).
notes: Applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents, except WASFA applicants. Most funds weigh financial need and/or academic achievement.

name: CFNLA scholarships
value: 10 named scholarships; the Community Bank Foundation Scholarship is $1,000; other amounts not listed.
deadline: 2027 deadlines not yet posted. 2026 deadlines were February 27, 2026 (Thomas E. McElroy, Jr.), March 27, 2026 (most funds) and March 28, 2026 (Community Bank Foundation).
apply: Apply through the CFNLA Scholarship Portal (GrantInterface) with transcripts, ACT scores and essays as each fund requires.
eligibility: Mostly seniors from specific schools or groups (for example C.E. Byrd, Homer or Haynesville high schools, or Barksdale AFB dependents). GPA minimums range from 2.5 to 3.4; some require ACT 20+, top 10% of class, or a science, engineering or geology major.
notes: Mostly merit-based; a few consider financial need.

name: CFGB scholarship process
value: Awards of about $1,000 to $6,000; about 3,000 Western New York students received about $3 million in 2025.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the process is currently closed.
apply: Apply through the Foundation's scholarship process when it opens (text SCHOLARSHIP to 855-628-3360 for alerts); submit the Student Aid Report, college award letters and grades.
eligibility: Permanent residents of Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Niagara, Orleans or Wyoming County with at least a C (2.0) average, accepted to an accredited nonprofit US school for full-time undergraduate study.
notes: Awards are based primarily on financial need, with preference for Pell-eligible students attending Western New York schools; some awards also weigh achievement or service.
